paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend: God is working even when it hurts. Micah 4:9-10 says Zion's anguish is like a woman in labor, and labor is pain that leads somewhere. She leaves the city and goes to Babylon, but the text says, "there the LORD will redeem you from the hand of your enemies!" (Micah 4:10). Hard seasons are not the end of the story when God is the One writing it.

Now look at the nations, because they thought they had the whole thing figured out. They wanted to feast their eyes on Zion, but Micah 4:12 says they "do not know the thoughts of the LORD or understand His plan." Friend, I've had batches go sideways that I thought were ruined, and the Lord was somewhere in the back going, "Oh, I've got this." What looks like the enemy winning may be a plan you can't see yet.

And then comes the little town, because God loves to start big things small. "But you, Bethlehem Ephrathah, who are small among the clans of Judah, out of you will come forth for Me One to be ruler over Israel" (Micah 5:2). This ruler will "stand and shepherd His flock in the strength of the LORD," and His people "will dwell securely" (Micah 5:4). So when you feel small or the siege feels loud, remember that He will be our peace (Micah 5:5), and that is why my ovens stay ready.
